title: Streeman and Blue Parody arrangements and singers
summary: Both bands used mostly stock arrangements; Streeman singers included Helen Englade and Jane Villegas, sister of Margaret Villegas who sang as Loretta Lee.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Yeah, well the cassettes never sounded as good to me. I was really disappointed. Yeah, I always like to hear the original if I can. Sure. Well, uh, was there any band that the Blue Parody in particular modeled itself on, or?
No, in fact, like I said before, the Blue Parody had a group, a good group. It was only out of the streaming group.
Mm-hmm. But did they have an arranger, or did they buy stocks, or?

No, no, it was all stocks and a few specials. Just like streaming operated. Mm-hmm. Streaming operated with 80% stock arrangements and about 20% of special arrangements. Streaming would have 10 or 12 special arrangements, maybe more. Or used to order them out of New York, you know. And Blue Parody was the same way. They played a lot of stocks and a few specials. Well, who did the singing? Oh. In the streaming band we had various singers. Helen, I'm trying to think of her last name. She was Miss New Orleans at one time. Yeah. And she left to sing with the Larry Clinton band. She sang with Al Stringer. Helen Englade, I was trying to think of her last name, who of course has since married and all that. But I think she won the Miss New Orleans contest, I believe, at one time. And she sang, and she later left with the Larry Clinton band. She traveled with Larry Clinton, I think she later married a man out of the Larry Clinton band, a sax player. And Jane Villegas sang with the Al Stringer band for a good while. Jane Villegas, her sister was Margaret Villegas. She just passed away recently. And Margaret Villegas was a professional singer who sang with some name bands, the George Hall band, big band, you know, traveled around the country. She sang under the name of Loretta Lee. And that was her kid sister Jane Villegas who used to sing with us. And the trumpet player that played, that I had the pleasure of working with, Irving Dusan, he's president of Columbia Homestead right now. It was a marvelous trumpet player. And I had the pleasure of working with Irving, with the Al Stringer band, for at least eight of the nineteen years he played with Al Stringer, a marvelous trumpet player.

No, he didn't sing, but he played a driving trumpet. He married Loretta Lee. I see. This professional singer who sang with George Hall and many named bands around the country. Her name was Margaret Villegas, and she just recently passed away within the last six, eight months of it.
I, I, I, I'm curious whether they added a, well you know they called them boy singers and girl singers in. Would they add any boy singers? Well they call them vocalists, so.
